answers.U1-S1: The narrator remembers his first long walk across the plain with his brother when he was young, before he could ride off alone to see the world.
answers.U1-S2: He was young and a bit scared and not very brave yet, since he was only six and not confident going far from home.
answers.U1-S3: To show how long and tiring the walk was for a little six-year-old boy, since they had to keep turning and push through tall grass.
answers.U1-S4: Seriously and slowly, in a calm, dignified way.
answers.U1-S5: Because the open wings were a bright crimson color he hadn't expected, which made the bird look even more beautiful.
answers.U1-S6: That the birds were rare there and unusual, something new nobody around them had seen before.
answers.U1-S7: Because it was so beautiful, tall, white and rose with glowing wings, that it seemed heavenly and amazing to him.
answers.U1-S8: He has seen flamingos hundreds of times in beautiful ways since, so they became familiar and never felt as new and special as the first time.
answers.U1-S9: It describes all the many times he later saw flamingos in different beautiful settings, like sunsets and flying flocks over blue water.
answers.U1-S10: He loves watching flamingos and admires their beauty, having seen them in all kinds of lovely scenes as a grown-up.
